Double Series and Fubini

Numbers on a grid get summed by rows first, then by columns, in this scene. With absolute convergence, the two answers agree.

Add along the rows or down the columns: the result is one and the same. The order cannot change it because the absolute values sum to a finite total. With only conditional convergence, swapping the order changes the answer itself. The headline value is the second formula below.

For example, stack 📦 boxes in a grid and count the items inside each box. Count row by row or column by column — the total count comes out identical.

  1. Fix a row (mmm fixed).

    The only nonzero entries are am,m=1a_{m,m} = 1am,m​=1 at n=mn = mn=m and am,m+1=−1a_{m,m+1} = -1am,m+1​=−1 at n=m+1n = m+1n=m+1.

    Hence the row sum is ∑n=1∞am,n=1+(−1)=0\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_{m,n} = 1 + (-1) = 0∑n=1∞​am,n​=1+(−1)=0 (a finite sum, so no convergence issue).

    This holds for every mmm, so ∑m=1∞∑n=1∞am,n=∑m=1∞0=0\sum_{m=1}^{\infty}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_{m,n} = \sum_{m=1}^{\infty} 0 = 0∑m=1∞​∑n=1∞​am,n​=∑m=1∞​0=0.

  2. Fix a column (nnn fixed).

    The nonzero entries: an,n=1a_{n,n} = 1an,n​=1 (row m=nm = nm=n) and, for n≥2n \ge 2n≥2, an−1,n=−1a_{n-1,n} = -1an−1,n​=−1 (row m=n−1m = n-1m=n−1, from am,m+1=−1a_{m,m+1} = -1am,m+1​=−1 with m=n−1m = n-1m=n−1).

    Column 111: only a1,1=1a_{1,1} = 1a1,1​=1, so the sum is 111.

    Column n≥2n \ge 2n≥2: 1+(−1)=01 + (-1) = 01+(−1)=0.

    Hence ∑n=1∞∑m=1∞am,n=1+∑n=2∞0=1\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\sum_{m=1}^{\infty} a_{m,n} = 1 + \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} 0 = 1∑n=1∞​∑m=1∞​am,n​=1+∑n=2∞​0=1.

  3. The two iterated sums differ, 0≠10 \ne 10=1 — the order changes the answer.

    The broken hypothesis is absolute convergence: ∑m,n∣am,n∣=∑n=1∞(1+1)=∞\sum_{m,n} \lvert a_{m,n}\rvert = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} (1 + 1) = \infty∑m,n​∣am,n​∣=∑n=1∞​(1+1)=∞, so the second problem's hypothesis fails.

    Without the nonnegative (or absolutely convergent) hypothesis Fubini fails, and this example shows the hypothesis is sharp.

    QED.
